headline: CULMINATION OF 65TH EDITION OF SUBROTO CUP INTERNATIONAL FOOTBALL TOURNAMENT 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

CULMINATION OF 65TH EDITION OF SUBROTO CUP INTERNATIONAL FOOTBALL TOURNAMENT 2026

24 SEP 2026 10:18PM by PIB Delhi

The 65th Subroto Cup International Football Tournament 2026 concluded at the Dr. BR Ambedkar Stadium, where Minerva Public School (MPS) CISCE, Mohali, defeated MIC EMHSS (Maqdoomiya Islamic Cultural English Medium Higher Secondary School), Kerala, by a score of 3–2 to claim the Junior Boys (U-17) championship title.

The high-intensity fixture opened with an early breakthrough from MPS Mohali, as Chetan Tiwari scored the opening goal in the 7th minute of play. MIC EMHSS responded in the final moments of the first half, with Thoufeeq scoring an equaliser during added time at the 37-minute mark to level the score going into the interval.

MPS Mohali established a decisive advantage early in the second half through two rapid goals. Punshiba Meitei restored the lead in the 40th minute, followed by a clinical finish from Md Azam Khan in the 46th minute, advancing the scoreline to 3–1.

MIC EMHSS mounted a late offensive, narrowing the deficit with a goal in the 65th minute. Despite sustained pressure from the Kerala team in the closing stages of the match, the MPS Mohali defence held firm to secure the 3–2 victory at the final whistle.

The final was graced by Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff and Chairman, Subroto Mukerjee Sports Education Society, who presented the trophy to the winners along with Shri Suresh Raina, Former Indian Cricket team member, who was the Guest of Honour for the finals.

Speaking during the prize distribution, Chief Guest Air Chief Marshal AP Singh complimented the players, participating schools, teams and sponsors for their contribution to the tournament. He emphasised the importance of encouraging sports at the grassroots level and said that participation and the spirit of playing are what matter most. He also complimented the finalists for an exciting and closely contested match. Thereafter, he declared the Subroto Cup International Football Tournament 2026 closed.

The winners received Rs 5,00,000 (Five Lakh) while the runner up received Rs 3,00,000 (Three Lakh) as prize money.

A total of 83 matches were played in this category of the Subroto Cup which was played at five venues in Delhi- Dr. Ambedkar Stadium, Tejas Football ground, Pinto Park Football ground, Subroto Football ground and Rajokri Football ground. Saint Patrick's High School, Gumla, Jharkhand emerged victorious in the Junior Girls (U-17) category defeating Springfield Higher Secondary School, NCC from Aizwal, while Manik Para Vivekanand Vidyapeeth, Jhargram, West Bengal won the Sub Junior Boys (U-15) category beating Kamrup Metropolitan Senior Secondary School, Assam in the finals which was held at Bengaluru:

headline: Climate Resilience, Water Finance and Innovation in Focus on Day 3 of India International Water Week 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

Climate Resilience, Water Finance and Innovation in Focus on Day 3 of India International Water Week 2026

Deliberations span climate risk assessment, early warning systems, glacial lake monitoring, water-use efficiency and innovative financing

India-Netherlands cooperation advances through two tripartite MoUs

24 SEP 2026 10:16PM by PIB Delhi

The third day carried the 9th India International Water Week 2026 deeper into its technical programme, into the forward-looking questions of climate risk, early warning, glacial lake monitoring, water pricing and the financing of resilient water infrastructure. Sessions ran in parallel across the Water Leaders' Forum, Country Forum, Practitioners' Forum, Thematic Forum and Start-Up Forum. The Thematic Forum closed the third of its seven sub-themes and moved through the fourth and fifth.

The day also widened the Week's international reach. The Start-Up Forum gave startups, MSMEs and academia a platform to pitch problem-driven water solutions. On the sidelines, a bilateral meeting advanced India-Netherlands cooperation, with two tripartite MoUs signed.

India-Netherlands Bilateral Meeting

On the sidelines of the 9th India International Water Week-2026, a bilateral meeting between the Shri C R Patil, Minister of Jal Shakti and H.E. Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice Minister for Infrastructure and Water Management, Netherlands, was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Minister of State, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Shri Ishwarsinh Patel, Minister of State for Water Resources and Water Supply (Independent Charge), joined the meeting, along with H. E Marissa Gerard, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to India.

During the event, a tripartite MoU was signed between Central Water Commission, Kalpasar, Deptt. Govt. of Gujarat and Deltares, Netherlands for technical support. Another tripartite MoU was signed between CWC, Kalpasar Deptt. of Govt. of Gujarat and TU Delft Netherlands for capacity building and trainings. The MoUs will facilitate technical collaboration through sharing of Dutch expertise and advanced engineering practices for the planning, design and implementation of the project.

Country Forum (CF)

CF-4 on Private Capital Mobilisation in the Water Sector, convened with the World Bank, was chaired by Shri Baldeo Purushartha, Joint Secretary, DEA, GOI and co-chaired by Smt. Roshika Singh, Principal Country Officer, IFC India. The session opened with a keynote by Shri Saroj Kumar Jha, Global Water Director, World Bank, and was moderated by Mr. William Rex, Practice Manager for Water, World Bank, with Jain Irrigations, IFC India, Coca-Cola,VA Tech Wabag, Tata Capital, the Maharashtra Institution for Transformation (MITRA) and the Uttar Pradesh State Transformation Commission, on the reforms and financing mechanisms needed to unlock private investment in urban water, wastewater and irrigation.

Water Leaders’ Forum (WLF)

WLF-3 on Improving Water Use Efficiency Using State-of-the-Art Technology in the Water Resources Sector, convened with the CII Water Institute, was chaired by P. C. Vyas, Principal Secretary, (Water Resources) Government of Gujarat, and co-chaired by Smt. Shilpa Nischal, Executive Director, CII Water Institute, with Grundfos, Murugappa Water Technology, Ion Exchange, Kritsnam Technologies and NITI Aayog, on smart metering, monitoring and technology for water-use efficiency.

WLF-4 on Climate Risk Assessment for Water Security, convened with the National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee, was chaired by Prof. Nagesh Kumar, Professor, IISc Bangalore, and co-chaired by Dr. Y. R. S. Rao, Director, NIH Roorkee, with ICHARM (Japan), IIT Bombay, IISc Bangalore, CWC and IIT Delhi, on integrating climate risk assessment into water governance and planning frameworks.

WLF-5 on Embedding Climate Action in Water Governance and Policies, convened with CEEW, was chaired by Shri Jogindra Singh IAS, Project Director, State Mission for Clean Ganga, Govt. of Uttar Pradesh, and co-chaired by Ms. Noa Amsalem, Water Attache, Embassy of Israel, with IIT Guwahati, WELL Labs Bengaluru, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Google, Council on Energy, Environment and Water and DCM Shriram, on shifting from managing climate risk to building resilience through governance reform.

WLF-6 on Climate-Resilient Adaptation Measures in Water Resources, convened with the National Dam Safety Authority was chaired by Shri Rakesh Kashyap, Chairman, National Dam Safety Authority and co-chaired by Shri Manoj Kumar Acharya, Former Chief Engineer, BODHI, Madhya Pradesh Water Resources Department, with IIT Delhi, HCL Foundation, IMD, GIZ and NDMA, addressed hydrological modelling for dams under a changing climate, glacial lake outburst floods, and the structural rehabilitation of earthen and rockfill dams, drawing on international financing experience for climate-resilient dam infrastructure.

Practitioners’ Forum (PF)

PF-5 on Session on Best Practices, convened with the National Water Mission, was chaired by Shri Rajesh Toppo, Secretary, Water Resources, Government of Chhattisgarh, and co-chaired by Shri Atul Jain, Former Chairman, Central Water Commission, with district collectors and municipal commissioners from Tripura, Telangana and Surat; and Himalayan Environmental Studies and Conservation Organization, Ministry of Rural Development and The Rainwater Project, on integrating global best practices with the Ministry of Jal Shakti's efforts; the Jal Jeevan Mission now reports about 81.5% of rural households with tap water connections.

PF-6 on Water Disputes and Resolution, was chaired by Dr. Srinivas Chokkakula, President and Chief Executive, Centre for Policy Research and co-chaired by Shri P. Dorje Gyamba, Chairman, Godavari River Management Board, with the CWC, Supreme Court advocates, the National Water Academy, Pune, and river-basin management board representatives, examined Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms and the proposed Disputes Resolution Committee under the Inter-State River Water Disputes framework.

PF-7 on Jal-Sanskriti and HARIT Pathways: India's Water Heritage for a Resilient Future, was chaired by Dr. Murli Manohar Joshi, Padma Vibhushan, Former Union Minister, Ministry of Human Resource Development, on connecting India's traditional water culture, its sacred rivers, temple tanks and stepwells, with modern, climate-resilient water management, and on carrying that heritage into community-led conservation.

Thematic Forum (TF)

Six Thematic Forum sessions ran through the day, presenting shortlisted papers, closing the third of the Forum's seven sub-themes and moving through the fourth and fifth.

Sub-theme 3 and Sub-theme 4, Water in Climate-Related Risk: TF-9 Data-Driven Governance, chaired by Shri Sher Singh, Chairman, Ganga Flood Control Commission and Member (Floods), CWC, and co-chaired by Shri S. G. Bhartariya, Member (SAM), Central Ground Water Board with the National Water Informatics Centre, BISAG-N and the Government of Andhra Pradesh; TF-10 Early Warning System for Climate Risk Reduction, chaired by Dr. Krishna Vatsa, Member, National Disaster Management Authority, and co-chaired by Dr. D.R. Pattanaik, Scientist-G, India Meteorological Department; TF-11 Monitoring of Glacial Lake Outburst, chaired by Shri D. P. Mathuria, Chief Engineer (P&DO), Central Water Commission, and co-chaired by Dr. Surjeet Singh, Scientist 'G' & Head Centre for Cryosphere & Climate Change Studies (C4S), NIH Roorkee; and TF-12 Climate Change: Erratic Precipitation, was chaired by Dr. D.S. Pai, Scientist-G, India Meteorological Department and co-chaired by Dr. Ankur Srivastava, Scientist E, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune with the India Meteorological Department, CWPRS Pune, NIH Roorkee and CWC. Papers ranged over water informatics and AI-assisted data governance, drought and flood forecasting, AI-powered dam-safety early warning, glacial lake outburst flood vulnerability and monitoring across the Himalaya, and long-term rainfall and temperature trends under a changing climate. Among the papers were the indigenous HIM JHEEL NETRA glacial-lake monitoring system, a national-scale flood forecasting system, erosion modelling on the Brahmaputra, and geophysical investigations for dam safety.

Sub-theme 5, Innovative Financing Models: TF-13 Public-Private Partnerships for Water Finance and Innovative Financing Models, was chaired by Mr. Takeshi Ueda, Director, South Asia, Sector Department 2, Agriculture, Food, Nature, and Rural Development Sector Group, Asian Development Bank with co-chair Shri Rajesh Advani, Senior Water Specialist, World Bank, with the Asian Development Bank; and TF-14 Policy for Water User Charges, was chaired by Shri Sanjay Marwah, Member, Haryana Water Resources Authority, and co-chaired by Shri Subrata Singh, Executive Director, Foundation for Ecological Society. Papers examined green finance for WASH infrastructure, solar power potential along the Ken-Betwa link, and the restructuring of water user charges, including a comparative analysis of CGWA guidelines and AI-based canal-release optimisation, and made the case for water user charges as a lever for the long-term sustainability of irrigation.

Start-Up Forum (SUF))

The Start-Up Forum, chaired by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology and co-chaired by Col. Saurabh Sanyal, Secretary General, ASSOCHAM showcased problem-driven solutions from startups, MSMEs and academia across water resources management, wastewater treatment, irrigation efficiency and smart water systems, including prototypes developed through partnerships between startups, industry and academia. The forum also provided startups with an opportunity to present practical, deployable solutions to a panel of experts and investors.

The Ministry has also strengthened engagement with academic institutions and students to provide them with first-hand exposure to the challenges and opportunities in the water sector.

After having several meetings with the AICTE in coordination with Ministry of Education last year, Jal Seva Adhyayan initiative is being implemented in collaboration with AICTE. 49 teams, comprising students and faculty, visited 132 villages across the country from February till April 2026. They gained first-hand exposure to rural drinking water service delivery and submitted detailed field reports based on their observations. Around 50 participating students also joined the Roundtable Conference with African Ambassadors at Bharat Mandapam. Following the roundtable, a special interaction session titled “Peyjal Ki Baat: Jal Shakti Minister ke Saath” was organised, providing students a unique opportunity to engage directly with the leadership of the Ministry of Jal Shakti and discuss challenges, innovations and opportunities in the water sector.

The interaction highlighted the importance of youth participation, innovation and community engagement in strengthening the country's water sector. Students were encouraged to take their learnings beyond the classroom, apply their technical knowledge to real-world challenges and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat 2047. The discussion focused on the transformative impact of the Jal Jeevan Mission on rural lives, the importance of safe drinking water, water quality surveillance through community participation, the growing role of digital technology and AI, and the need for innovative, practical and scalable solutions to address emerging water-sector challenges.

Addressing the students, Shri C R Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, emphasised that the Jal Jeevan Mission is not merely an infrastructure programme but a transformational initiative linked to health, dignity, women's empowerment and quality of life. He urged students to develop innovative and cost-effective technological solutions for the water sector and stressed the importance of dialogue and consensus in resolving water-related challenges.

Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Jal Shakti, encouraged students to study global best practices, leverage AI, digital technologies and social media, and identify solutions emerging from rural communities and grassroots innovators.

Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, underlined the need to expose engineering students to ground-level realities of rural water supply systems and informed that, in collaboration with AICTE, efforts are underway to introduce water governance-related academic courses and expand the outreach of Jal Seva Adhyayan to engineering institutions nationwide.

Smt. Archana Varma, Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources, highlighted the transformative potential of information technology and artificial intelligence in water governance and called upon students to apply their technical expertise in public service, innovation and sustainable water management for national development.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission, welcomed the panelists and the students to the interactive session. He briefed about the Jal Seva Adhyayan, and the upcoming water management course by AICTE.

Technical Sessions

The first technical session, “Water Supply Systems: O&M, Infrastructure & Source Sustainability,” focused on strengthening the long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems. Four papers were presented covering themes including GIS-based assessment of water supply infrastructure, water pricing strategies, water footprint assessment for sustainable water resources management, and approaches to strengthening community ownership in piped drinking water systems. The discussions highlighted the importance of effective operation and maintenance, infrastructure and asset management, financial sustainability, and community participation in ensuring reliable water services.

The second technical session, “Water Quality, Safety & Emerging Contaminants,” focused on water safety and quality management in the context of emerging challenges. Five papers examined community-led climate-resilient interventions for water security, evaluation of field test kits for water safety planning, emerging contaminants and environmental laws, water quality challenges in India, and the use of digital tools for tracking water refill stations. The presentations highlighted the need for stronger water quality monitoring, water safety planning, community participation, and technology-enabled approaches.

Another session, “Financing, Economic Models & Techno-Economic Solutions,” deliberated on approaches to improving the financial and technological sustainability of water and sanitation services. Four papers covered innovative models for rural water supply, wastewater treatment and cost recovery, local economic models for sustaining rural drinking water services, and low-cost atmospheric water harvesting solutions. The session highlighted the role of appropriate technologies, local economic models, capacity building, and innovative approaches in supporting sustainable water services.

The fourth technical session, “Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions & Sanitation/Other,” focused on approaches for strengthening the resilience of WASH systems in the face of climate-related challenges. Four papers covered digital intelligence and machine learning applications in sewage sludge management, sanitation innovation through start-ups and public-private partnerships, approaches to building water consciousness, and AI-enabled mechanised and robotic operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructure. The discussions highlighted the role of technology, innovation, partnerships and systems strengthening in addressing emerging challenges in water and sanitation.

(Release ID: 2314659)

headline: DRI seizes 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 15 crore at Mumbai airport; three arrested
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 15 crore at Mumbai airport; three arrested

Gold powder ingeniously blended with food products like milk powder, oats, rice flour and cake mix

25 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai Zonal Unit, based on specific intelligence, intercepted three Indian passengers arriving from Dubai at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, in the early hours of 23.09.2026, with operational assistance from the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU), Mumbai Airport Customs.

Detailed examination of their baggage revealed a highly sophisticated and unusual method of concealment, wherein foreign-origin gold had been converted into fine powder and meticulously mixed with packaged food products of similar colour, texture and consistency to evade detection.

The gold powder was found concealed across several apparently ordinary food packets like milk powder, oats, various flours, Nutella and coconut milk powder. In all, approximately 33.50 kg food products mixed with gold powder were recovered from the baggage of the three passengers.

Through careful segregation and assaying, 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold, valued at approximately Rs. 14.81 crore, was recovered and seized under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962. During questioning, all three passengers admitted to acting on behalf of the same organised gold-smuggling syndicate. They were accordingly arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

The operation has uncovered a novel and sophisticated method of gold smuggling, wherein powdered gold was ingeniously blended with a wide variety of packaged food products to evade routine detection.

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai Zonal Unit, seized 9.40 kg of foreign‑origin gold worth approximately Rs. 14.81 crore from three Indian passengers arriving from Dubai at Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport on 23 September 2026. headline: DRI seizes over 125,000 kg foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts and 41,000 kg poppy seeds worth around Rs. 20.31 crore in Assam and Mizoram in a crackdown on cross-border smuggling; four arrested
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes over 125,000 kg foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts and 41,000 kg poppy seeds worth around Rs. 20.31 crore in Assam and Mizoram in a crackdown on cross-border smuggling; four arrested

This is one of the largest seizure of smuggled areca nuts in North-East Region

25 SEP 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on cross-border smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized 1,25,680 kg of foreign-origin areca nuts and 41,697 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds, collectively valued at approximately Rs. 20.31 crore, in two intelligence-led operations in Mizoram and Assam. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the transportation of the smuggled poppy seeds.

On 23-24.09.26, in a major intelligence led operation in Mizoram, DRI with the assistance of Customs Champhai, 14th Battalion Assam Rifles and Champhai Police, searched three godowns in and around Ruantlang village, Champhai District, located approximately 20 km from the Indo-Myanmar border. All the premises were found locked and unattended. The search of the premises resulted in the recovery of 1,25,680 kg suspected foreign-origin areca nuts valued at around Rs. 14 Crore and 25,440 kg of poppy seeds valued at Rs. 3.81 crore. Preliminary investigation indicated that the goods had been smuggled into India from Myanmar. The goods were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Earlier on 22.09.26, based on specific intelligence regarding transportation of foreign-origin poppy seeds from the Mizoram border area towards Assam, DRI officers with the assistance of 38 Battalion Assam Rifles, intercepted two trucks near Lailapur, Silchar. Detailed examination and rummaging of the vehicles resulted in the recovery of 290 HDPE bags containing 16,257 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds. The bags bore markings indicative of foreign manufacture and trade, and the consignment was not accompanied by valid import documents. The poppy seeds, valued at approximately Rs 2.43 crore, along with the two vehicles, were seized under the Customs Act, 1962. Four persons involved in the transportation were arrested.

The seizure of foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts, one of the largest seizures of the commodity in recent years in the North-Eastern region of the country, is a significant achievement in DRI’s efforts to curb cross-border smuggling.

Poppy seeds are classified as a “Restricted” item under the ITC (HS) Classification of the Foreign Trade Policy, with import permitted subject to specified conditions, including sourcing from designated countries and registration of import contracts with the Narcotics Commissioner, Gwalior.

The seizures highlight DRI’s continued focus on intercepting smuggling networks operating through the vulnerable India-Myanmar border and preventing illicit entry of restricted and foreign-origin agricultural commodities into the country.

headline: A Glimpse into Odisha’s Rich Cultural Legacy at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

A Glimpse into Odisha’s Rich Cultural Legacy at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026

From representations of Lord Jagannath to Pattachitra, Tarakasi and Sambalpuri art, the collection brings together several distinctive expressions of Odisha’s cultural identity.

25 SEP 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

Odisha’s diverse cultural heritage takes center stage in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with a collection of artefacts showcasing the state’s traditions of devotion, craftsmanship, painting, textiles and literature. The catalogue features a wide range of works centered on Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Devi Subhadra, alongside representations of Odisha’s regional deities, traditional art forms, textiles, festivals and prominent cultural figures.

Among the notable pieces is a Jagannath Parivar on Chariot, depicting Lord Jagannath, Devi Subhadra and Lord Balabhadra seated on an intricately detailed chariot drawn by four sculpted horses, a representation of the cultural and spiritual significance of Rath Yatra.

The collection also includes a Pattachitra painting depicting the Puri Rath Yatra, portraying the deities in their chariot amid scenes of dance, music and celebration, highlighting the work's intricate detailing, vibrant colours and connection with Odisha's devotional artistic traditions.

The auction catalogue also showcases several traditional crafts associated with the state. Among them are works in Cuttack silver filigree or Tarakasi, an intricate craft involving delicate silver wires, as well as Sambalpuri textiles and Ikat.

Another featured work is a Maa Samaleswari devotional icon created using Sambalpuri Ikat, with the artwork entirely hand-woven through the traditional Bandha technique.

Beyond Jagannath-themed works, the collection captures Odisha's vibrant festival traditions. A framed print documents the Panchu Dola Melana, showing devotees carrying colourful miniature temple structures, while another photograph captures the festival at Chilika Lake, featuring boats carrying village deities for their annual gathering.

Taken together, the 62 mementos present a broad visual narrative of Odisha, from the enduring traditions of Jagannath worship and Rath Yatra to Pattachitra, Tarakasi, Sambalpuri Ikat, regional festivals and literary heritage. Rather than representing a single artistic tradition, the catalogue brings together multiple expressions of the state's living cultural heritage in one collection.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 is live until 2 October 2026. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: pmmementos.gov.in

fullText:
Ministry of Education

India’s innovation surge will drive the vision of Viksit Bharat: Shri Pralhad Joshi

When innovation begins with a real human need and leads to a practical solution, it becomes an act of ‘Seva’: Shri Pralhad Joshi

Union Minister for Education inaugurates Seva First Innovation Challenge at IISc Bengaluru

25 SEP 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today urged the youth to combine the spirit of ‘Seva’ with innovation to identify real-life challenges and develop practical, scalable solutions. This would enable their participation and contribution in fulfilling the vision of Viksit Bharat, 2047. The Minister stated this while inaugurating the Seva First Innovation Challenge (SFIC) for the South Zone at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. The Minister also launched the website and registration portal for SFIC.

The Minister said, “Seva must find expression in action,” adding that understanding a problem and finding an innovative solution to address it at scale was an important expression of service. Highlighting India’s demographic dividend, Shri Joshi noted that nearly 65 per cent of India’s population was below the age of 35. He said India had a generation that was curious, confident, and comfortable with technology. He added that there was a responsibility to give young people opportunities to turn that curiosity into useful action.

Referring to the role and importance of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Shri Pralhad Joshi mentioned that NEP placed critical thinking, creativity, experiential learning and problem-solving at the heart of education. He noted that this vision was being translated into opportunities for students to experiment, build and innovate from an early age. He also highlighted the Government’s efforts to build a strong innovation ecosystem through more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs, 17,300 odd Institutions Innovation Councils and initiatives such as Smart India Hackathon.

The Minister emphasised that innovation guided by the spirit of Seva could contribute meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He also called upon start-ups and industry partners to engage with young innovators emerging from the Challenge and encouraged the creation of a national repository through the SFIC website to support future mentoring, adoption, and scaling of promising solutions. He congratulated IISc Bengaluru, participating institutions, faculty members, start-ups and all stakeholders associated with the Initiative and said that he expected to see the strongest solutions from across India at the National Finale in New Delhi in December 2026.

IISc Bengaluru will serve as the South Zone Nodal Institute, supporting technical evaluation and mentorship across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.

SFIC will bring together students and young innovators from schools, ITIs, polytechnics, colleges and universities across five national themes (1. Clean and Sustainable Bharat, 2. Prosperous Farmers, Prosperous Bharat, 3. Healthy and Inclusive Bharat, 4. Educated and Skilled Bharat and 5. Secure Bharat) and two solution tracks (Track A — Product or Technology Solution and Track B — Business Model or Governance Solution). The Challenge aims to take promising ideas beyond submission through mentoring, incubation and pathways for real-life adoption. The Challenge will remain open for registration from September 25 to October 24, 2026, with the National Finale scheduled in New Delhi in December 2026.

headline: TRAI Launches Digital Connectivity Rating Platform
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

TRAI Launches Digital Connectivity Rating Platform

25 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform, an integrated digital platform designed to provide visibility of rating of properties to the consumers and facilitate the end-to-end process for rating the digital connectivity of properties along with a mobile app for testing digital connectivity.

The DCR Platform facilitates implementation of the framework prescribed under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity) Regulations, 2024, as amended by the Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, notified on 13 May 2026 and rating process specified in Rating Manual 2026, issued by TRAI on 9 June 2026.

The platform provides a public interface for consumers to view the properties rated for digital connectivity. It brings Property Managers (PMs) registered Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA) and consumer onto a common digital interface. Property Managers can register their properties in category of Public, Government, Commercial, Private etc., submit rating applications, upload the prescribed information and documents, select a registered DCRA and track the status of their application through the platform. The platform supports the prescribed assessment workflow for both constructed and under-construction properties. Registered DCRAs can access assigned applications, undertake assessments, record observations and test results, manage supporting documentation and complete the rating process in accordance with the prescribed framework. The platform enables the digital workflow relating to assessment, report generation, certification and publication of ratings. Consumers and other stakeholders will be able to search rated properties, view published ratings, verify the corresponding certificates and compare the properties of interest.

Field assessments will be facilitated through a dedicated DCRA mobile app. The app will enable authorised DCRA to undertake in-building digital connectivity measurements in accordance with the prescribed testing methodology. Property information received through the web portal and the assessment data captured through the mobile application will be synchronised in the platform. The platform integrates eSign for the digital signing and verification of documents and certificates. It also supports online payment of applicable rating fees, email and SMS alerts, and secure storage of property records, test results, certificates and audit logs.

For Consumers, the platform offers a public rating search page. Consumers can search for a rated property by property name, certificate ID or location. They can view the property’s digitally signed rating certificate and verify its authenticity through the QR code provided on the certificate. This will make digital connectivity a visible and verifiable attribute of a rated property and empowers consumers with connectivity information. Based on this information consumer can make an informed choice while selecting the desired property prior to making the final purchase or lease decision.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI, said, “The Digital Connectivity Rating Platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties. By making ratings publicly searchable and verify the certificates, the platform will empower consumers with credible and comparable information. It will help them make more informed choices about homes and offices with strong and reliable connectivity, supporting smoother calls, downloads and access to online services. It will also enable consumers to recognise the value of digital connectivity infrastructure built into a property, while encouraging Property Managers to plan such infrastructure at the appropriate stage of property development.”

About the Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Framework

The DCR framework provides a standardised method for evaluating digital connectivity within properties. The assessment considers prescribed parameters relating to fibre readiness, mobile network availability, in-building solutions and Wi-Fi infrastructure, with applicable benchmarks for different categories of properties. The framework seeks to encourage the consideration of Digital Connectivity Infrastructure at appropriate stages of property development and facilitate the assessment of infrastructure and connectivity performance in existing properties. The Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform can be accessed at: https://dcrp.trai.gov.in

For additional queries, please contact: Ms. Archna Ahlawat, Advisor (IT) at advisorit@trai.gov.in

The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under the Union Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, conducted an Eleven-Day Training of Trainers (ToT) Programme for Master Trainers for the “Geriatric Care Provider” Job Role, at NISD at Dwarka in the National Capital here.

Organized by the Senior Citizen Division (Sr.CD), NISD of the Ministry from September 7 to 18, 2026, the programme aimed to strengthen quality, standardization and professional competency in geriatric care training and to create a national pool of trained and certified Master Trainers capable of delivering high-quality, competency-based training to geriatric caregivers across the country.

A Senior Official at NISD said the programme brought together participants from diverse professional backgrounds, including GNM, B.Sc. Nursing, Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing, M.Sc. Nursing and MBBS, thereby facilitating a multidisciplinary learning environment relevant to the care, health and well-being of senior citizens.

He informed that during the inaugural session, Dr. H.C. Sridhara Channakeshava Ranga Reddy, Deputy Director, Senior Citizen Division, NISD, outlined the objectives and significance of the Training of Trainers programme.

Dr Ranga Reddy elaborated on the roles, responsibilities, qualities and competencies expected of Master Trainers and emphasised the importance of integrating Domain Skills and Platform Skills for effective delivery of competency-based geriatric care training.

The NISD Official informed that the ToT programme was structured around two key components namely Domain Skills and Platform Skills. He said the Domain Skills component focused on professional competencies required for the Geriatric Care Provider job role, while Platform Skills strengthened participants’ capabilities in communication, facilitation, instructional delivery, learner engagement, training methodologies and assessment practices.

The Official further said the programme covered a comprehensive range of subjects relevant to geriatric care, including age-related changes in body systems and associated health concerns; healthy and active ageing; caregiving procedures; preventive healthcare; geriatric nutrition; communication and companionship; dementia care; mental health among older persons; prevention and management of non-communicable diseases; ageing with dignity; first aid and emergency care; yoga and meditation; caregiver self-care; and employability skills.

He further informed that the participants were also oriented to assessment requirements, documentation procedures, competency standards and certification processes, with emphasis on ensuring uniformity, consistency and quality in the delivery of geriatric care training programmes.

Talking about the Expert-led, Participatory Training Methodology, the Official said a distinguished panel of experts and resource persons from geriatric care and allied sectors conducted specialised and interactive sessions throughout the programme.

Ms. Jasmine Hussain facilitated sessions on Platform Skills, while Dr. Gahan S. Jois, Dr. K.S. Baghotia, Mr. Prem Poddar, Mr. Arvind Narayanan, Mr. R. Narendar, Mr. Vishnu Shankar, Ms. Deeika Sharma, Ms. Sudha Jhijaria and Ms. Tejasvini conducted sessions covering various Domain Skill areas, including dementia care and management, mental health, prevention and control of non-communicable diseases, ageing with dignity, yoga, meditation, and first aid and emergency care.

The NISD Official informed that the training followed a participatory, competency-based and practice-oriented approach, incorporating expert lectures, interactive discussions, role plays, hands-on exercises, practical demonstrations, group activities, case-based learning and experience sharing. He said the methodology was designed to strengthen not only participants’ technical knowledge but also their capacity to effectively impart knowledge and skills to future geriatric caregivers.

The Official said the programme concluded with the distribution of certificates among the participants adding that the participants expressed their satisfaction over the structured, interactive and practice-oriented methodology and highlighted its relevance in strengthening professional standards and improving the quality of geriatric care training.

He said the programme further reinforces NISD’s commitment to promoting dignified, compassionate and quality care for senior citizens and supporting the development of a robust and professional care ecosystem in India.

The Official said through initiatives such as the Training of Trainers Programme, the National Institute of Social Defence continues to promote capacity building, skill development and standardization in the elderly care sector. The initiative contributes towards developing a skilled, certified and quality-oriented geriatric care workforce capable of responding to the evolving care needs of India’s growing senior citizen population.

It is pertinent to mention that NISD has been recognized as an Awarding Body by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), marking an important milestone in strengthening the vocational education and training ecosystem in the field of social defence, particularly in the area of geriatric care.

Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, held a meeting today in New Delhi with Mr. Bernard Fontana, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, EDF, France, to review the ongoing engagement between India and EDF on the proposed deployment of EPR reactors in India. EDF apprised the Indian side of its efforts to build an ecosystem and supply chain in India for large-scale localization, and reiterated that a sizeable programme with multiple nuclear reactors would give suppliers confidence and enable economies of scale by leveraging Indian industry's capabilities.

Secretary (Power) briefed the French side on the progress made in finalizing India's regulatory framework for the nuclear power sector, including the Draft SHANTI (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India) Rules and Regulations, placed by the Department of Atomic Energy in the public domain for stakeholder consultation. The Rules provide for a streamlined, time-bound licensing framework and enable participation of private and foreign partners in India's nuclear power programme.

The two sides also discussed cooperation on pumped hydro storage projects, building on the proposed NTPC-EDF joint venture in this area.

headline: APEDA Facilitates Export of GI-Tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to Maldives
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

APEDA Facilitates Export of GI-Tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to Maldives

Export-Linked Channel Enables Farmer Realisation of ₹82 per kg Against Prevailing Market Price of ₹60 per kg

25 SEP 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a 1 MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives on 24 September 2026. The initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brands in agri exports.

A key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers. While the prevailing market price is ₹60 per kg, farmer realisation through the export-linked channel is ₹82 per kg, representing more than 30 per cent higher realisation. The initiative also provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets.

The consignment, exported by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its FPO-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea.

Gulbarga Tur Dal, associated with the Kalaburagi region of Karnataka, received Geographical Indication (GI) registration in 2019. The product is recognised for its distinctive taste and quality and forms an important part of the agricultural economy of the region. APEDA lists Gulbarga Tur Dal among Karnataka’s registered GI products.

Karnataka is one of India’s major agricultural states, with pulses playing an important role in its dryland agriculture and rural economy. Kalaburagi is one of the major centres of tur cultivation and production in the state, and Gulbarga Tur Dal represents the region’s distinctive agricultural identity.

Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, highlighted the importance of taking India’s GI-tagged agricultural products to global markets and creating stronger market linkages for farmers. He said the export of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives provides an opportunity to build the product’s global identity while opening avenues for further market expansion.

The export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. It will also support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

The consignment was flagged off in the presence of Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev. Senior APEDA officers and industry representatives, including Senior Consultant, APEDA Dr. Tarun Bajaj; General Manager, APEDA Smt. Vinita Sudhanshu, Managing Director KSPAML, Gulbarga Shri V. Sadashiva; and Shri Imran Pasha of M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, attended the event.

The initiative is aligned with APEDA’s efforts to facilitate exports of GI-tagged and other value-added agricultural products to international markets and reflects the scope for promoting region-specific agricultural products through international trade.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Arogya Manthan 2026, marking eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Arogya Manthan 2026, marking eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM

AB PM-JAY and ABDM Milestones Reflect India’s Expanding Digital and Health Assurance Ecosystem: Shri J.P. Nadda

AB PM-JAY Emerges as World’s Largest Health Assurance Programme, Covering Over 60 Crore Beneficiaries: Union Health Minister

Arogya Manthan 2026 launches a series of digital health and health assurance initiatives, including National Healthcare Providers Registry Mobile App, Secure Data Environment and Auto-Adjudication Framework for AB PM-JAY

Arogya Manthan 2026 recognises States and Union Territories for excellence in implementation of AB PM-JAY and ABDM across various categories

25 SEP 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda, today inaugurated Aarogya Manthan 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, marking eight years of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) and five y ears of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). Organised by the National Health Authority (NHA), the event brought together senior government officials, healthcare providers, insurers, technology and digital health experts, academia, development partners and other stakeholders to deliberate on the progress of India’s health assurance and digital health ecosystem and the priorities for its next phase.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda, congratulated all stakeholders on the completion of eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of ABDM. He said that these milestones provide an opportunity to take stock of the progress made and renew the commitment towards the welfare of the poor and marginalised sections of society, in line with the hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas.”

Shri Nadda highlighted the significant expansion of AB PM-JAY since its inception and said that the scheme has emerged as the world’s largest health assurance programme, with more than 60 crore beneficiaries covered and over 13 crore hospital admissions facilitated, involving treatment worth more than Rs. 2 lakh crores.

He noted that the Government further expanded the scheme to cover all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status, bringing them within its ambit. He also highlighted the importance of portability under the scheme, particularly for migrant workers, and appreciated the contribution of State Governments, healthcare institutions and other stakeholders in taking the programme forward.

The Union Minister said that the journey of AB PM-JAY and ABDM has demonstrated the transformative role of technology in healthcare, with digital systems supporting authentication, authorisation and access to treatment across locations. Highlighting the progress under ABDM, he said that more than 97.8 crore ABHAs have been created, with over 121 crore health records linked, while more than 5.6 lakh health facilities and around 11 lakh healthcare professionals are registered on the ABDM ecosystem. He also highlighted the development of the National Health Claims Exchange, which seeks to bring hospitals and insurers onto a common digital platform.

Referring to the initiatives launched at Aarogya Manthan 2026, Shri Nadda said that these would further strengthen digital healthcare, facilitate the secure use of health data and create new opportunities for health research, innovation and data-driven decision-making. He appreciated the National Health Authority and acknowledged the role of State Governments, healthcare professionals, empanelled hospitals, Ayushman Mitras, ASHA and Anganwadi workers, technology partners and other stakeholders.

Shri Nadda emphasised that the journey must continue and called for sustained efforts to leverage digital technology to make healthcare more accessible, efficient and patient-centric. He expressed confidence that the deliberations at Aarogya Manthan 2026 would generate actionable outcomes and contribute further towards strengthening India’s health ecosystem and serving humanity.

Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), Niti Ayoga, congratulated the National Health Authority (NHA) on the occasion. Highlighting the transformation brought about by AB PM-JAY, he said that the scheme has enabled people, particularly from economically weaker sections, to access healthcare with greater confidence and reduced financial burden. He emphasised that the next phase should focus on strengthening continuity of care, quality and patient-centric healthcare, including seamless referral mechanisms for patients requiring specialised treatment.

Dr. Srinivas highlighted the importance of achieving wider adoption and saturation of ABHA and strengthening interoperability of digital health records, with citizen consent and appropriate safeguards. He stressed that high-quality, standardised and interoperable health data would be critical for advancing health research and responsibly leveraging Artificial Intelligence in healthcare. He also called for strengthening the National Health Claims Exchange, improving ease of claims and pre-authorisation processes, and expanding awareness of health assurance and digital health initiatives.

Shri Ajay Seth, Chairman, IRDAI, highlighted the success of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and said that the experience gained through the scheme provides an opportunity to further strengthen the health insurance ecosystem in the country. He emphasised the need to ensure quality, affordability and access in healthcare while creating value for all stakeholders, including citizens, hospitals, insurers and technology providers.

Highlighting the importance of standardisation and transparency in health insurance, Shri Seth underlined the need for wider adoption of key digital and operational building blocks, including ABHA as an identity for health insurance, codification of treatments, standard billing formats, and standard treatment protocols and guidelines. He also highlighted the role of India’s digital public infrastructure and the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX) in enabling greater interoperability and creating a more connected health insurance ecosystem. He said, “It is within our reach to provide effective healthcare for the widest possible population — affordable and with good quality.”

Speaking at the Occasion, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, DG ICMR & Secretary DHR, highlighted the significance of the eight-year milestone of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and five years of ABDM, noting that Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has emerged as the world’s largest health assurance scheme, covering and benefiting more than 60 crore citizens. He said the focus going forward would be on further improving the quality of healthcare and expanding coverage to ensure greater benefits for citizens.

Highlighting the collaboration between DHR, ICMR and NHA, Dr Bahl outlined two key areas of work. On standardisation of treatment, he noted that treatment based on standardised algorithms can help ensure greater consistency and quality of care, with ICMR having developed more than 150 standard treatment workflows and guidelines. He also highlighted the importance of cost-effectiveness in healthcare, noting that the Health Technology Assessment in India (HTAIn) under DHR evaluates the cost-effectiveness of healthcare technologies and interventions.

Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, NHA, congratulated all stakeholders on achieving two significant milestones — eight years of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and five years of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). He highlighted the scale and reach of both programmes, with over 49 crore Ayushman Cards and around 98 crore ABHA IDs generated across the country.

Looking ahead, he noted that Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has generated more than 13 crore patient records, creating a valuable repository for research, development and health analytics. He said the Secure Data Environment will enable responsible use of such data while safeguarding patient identities. He also highlighted the launch of the Auto-Adjudication Framework, aimed at streamlining and strengthening the claims adjudication process under AB PM-JAY through technology and data-driven processes.

A major highlight of Arogya Manthan 2026 was the launch of a series of initiatives aimed at strengthening the digital foundations of India’s health assurance ecosystem. These included the National Healthcare Providers Registry (NHPR) Mobile App, NHCX Implementation Guide for Payers, Guidebook for a Model Digital Health Facility, Secure Data Environment (SDE) application and Framework for Auto-Adjudication of Claims under AB PM-JAY.

The Secure Data Environment, developed by the National Health Authority (NHA) with the support of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, is envisaged as a governed environment for access to and analysis of AB PM-JAY and ABDM health data. Approved entities will be able to work with de-identified data or execute code within an isolated NHA environment, with outputs reviewed before release. The initiative is intended to facilitate health research, programme planning, outcome analysis and responsible AI innovation, while incorporating safeguards for protection of personal data.

The deliberations at Arogya Manthan 2026 focused on strengthening the efficiency, quality and interoperability of health services. The session on “NHCX for Streamlining Health Insurance” examined the role of the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX) in enabling streamlined, standardised and technology-driven health insurance processes, including how interoperable digital claims infrastructure can improve efficiency, strengthen coordination across the health insurance ecosystem, and open new avenues of health financing.

This was followed by parallel sessions under the AB PM-JAY and ABDM tracks, examining key aspects of programme implementation, healthcare delivery and digital transformation.

Under the AB PM-JAY track, the session on “Claim Processing to Intelligent Assurance: Transforming AB PM-JAY” examined the use of technology, data and analytics for strengthening claims processing and programme integrity. The session on “Strategic Purchasing from the Perspective of Quality and Cost-Effectiveness” discussed approaches to improving quality of care while promoting efficient utilisation of resources.

The ABDM track included discussions on “UHI for Improving Access of Healthcare Services”, focusing on the role of digital platforms in expanding access and participation across the healthcare ecosystem, and “Leveraging Standards for Better Health Delivery”, which examined the importance of common health-data standards for seamless exchange of information and improved continuity and quality of healthcare delivery.

The event also recognised States and Union Territories for their performance under AB PM-JAY and ABDM across different categories. Under AB PM-JAY, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim and Jammu & Kashmir were recognised for the highest card saturation among ASHA, Anganwadi Worker (AWW) and Anganwadi Helper (AWH) beneficiaries in the large State, small State and Union Territory categories, respectively. Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat were recognised as the top-performing States in claim settlement for inter-State portability.

Under ABDM, Bihar, Ladakh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli were recognised as top-performing States/UTs across model districts based on district population categories. Chandigarh, Assam and Uttar Pradesh were recognised for the highest number of sub-centres using ABDM-enabled Health Management Information Systems (HMIS) in the small State/UT, medium State/UT and large State categories, respectively.

headline: Union MoS for Health & Family Welfare Smt. Anupriya Patel addresses 71st Foundation Day celebrations of AIIMS New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union MoS for Health & Family Welfare Smt. Anupriya Patel addresses 71st Foundation Day celebrations of AIIMS New Delhi

Medical colleges rise from 387 to over 800 and undergraduate medical seats from 51,000 to nearly 1.3 lakh: Smt. Anupriya Patel

Smt. Patel calls upon AIIMS New Delhi to lead advanced clinical care, nurture healthcare professionals and guide the expanding AIIMS network

AIIMS New Delhi has a special responsibility as the apex mentor for medical institutions across the country: Smt. Anupriya Patel

Smt. Patel emphasizes that technology must complement, not replace, human clinical judgement and care; stresses the health and well-being of healthcare professionals

Smt. Anupriya Patel inaugurates ‘AIIMS: Seven Decades of Healthcare Innovation’ exhibition showcasing seven decades of milestones and achievements

Over 1,500 school students to participate in health education and community outreach activities at the AIIMS exhibition

25 SEP 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel addressed the 71st Foundation Day celebrations of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, as the Chief Guest today. The celebrations marked over seven decades of AIIMS’ contributions to healthcare, medical education, research and innovation.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Anupriya Patel said that “since its inception in 1956, AIIMS New Delhi has occupied a special place in the healthcare journey of the country.” She highlighted its contribution to redefining medical education, pioneering groundbreaking research and delivering high-quality patient care. She underlined that “over the decades, the name AIIMS has become synonymous with clinical excellence and public trust.” She noted that while the institution has a distinguished legacy, this legacy also brings greater responsibility for the future and requires continued focus on national healthcare priorities.

Smt. Patel highlighted the transformation of India’s healthcare and medical education landscape. She noted that the country has expanded from one AIIMS at the turn of the century to a network of 23 AIIMS institutions. Since 2014, the number of medical colleges has increased from 387 to over 800, while undergraduate medical seats have increased from 51,000 to nearly 1.3 lakh, along with a substantial expansion in postgraduate opportunities.” She further added that the Government envisions adding another 75,000 medical seats to further strengthen this framework. This expansion is not merely a matter of numbers but is closely linked to equity and access.”

Smt. Patel further emphasized that “quality medical education must reach every region, advanced tertiary healthcare must be brought closer to citizens, and the country must build a strong pool of doctors, nurses, scientists and allied healthcare professionals capable of responding to changing demographic and epidemiological needs.” She added that “AIIMS New Delhi has a special responsibility in this transformation as the apex mentor and as an institution that has established a benchmark for the rest of the country.”

Speaking about the scale of healthcare services at AIIMS New Delhi, Smt. Patel said that the institution’s enormous clinical volume should not be viewed merely through statistics. Millions of outpatient visits represent individuals and families placing their trust in the institution, while admissions and surgeries represent situations in which patients entrust their lives to its doctors, nurses and support staff. She emphasised that AIIMS is therefore not only a centre of medical excellence but also an institution of public trust, and that this trust has to be earned and nurtured every day.

Smt. Patel also highlighted AIIMS’ role at the forefront of advanced medical care and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), robotic surgery, organ transplantation and advanced diagnostics. She emphasised that “technology must remain an instrument for better patient care and should complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgement.” She noted that “AI cannot replace a physician’s intuition, a robotic arm cannot replace a surgeon’s judgement, and technology cannot replace the reassuring human presence of a nurse.” She stressed the importance of maintaining a balance between scientific advancement and the human touch in healthcare.

She also underlined that quality healthcare must also be reflected in the patient’s overall experience. She called for the AIIMS premises to be made more navigable for citizens and emphasised the importance of empathy, clear communication, dignity and patient-centred care. She also referred to the importance of patient safety and the collective responsibility of doctors, nurses, technicians and administrative personnel in ensuring safe and quality healthcare.

Smt. Patel emphasised that expansion of healthcare infrastructure must go hand in hand with quality. She noted that a new ward requires adequate nursing support, specialised services require trained professionals and digital initiatives should help reduce friction for patients. She stressed that growth and quality must progress together and that AIIMS New Delhi should continue to demonstrate that expansion in scale can coexist with high standards of patient care.

Highlighting the growing importance of preventive healthcare, Smt. Patel said that India’s health priorities increasingly focus on prevention, early detection and timely management, particularly in the context of non-communicable and lifestyle-related diseases. Referring to the shift in the policy approach towards prevention and health promotion, she called upon AIIMS to leverage its intellectual capital to contribute to public health policy, community health, lifestyle management and preventive medicine.

Smt. Patel also underlined the importance of the National Health Policy, 2017, and the broader shift towards preventive and promotive healthcare. She said that healthcare must address the country’s changing epidemiological burden while ensuring that citizens have access to affordable and quality services.

Highlighting the role of Ayushman Bharat and Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) in expanding access to healthcare and protecting vulnerable families from the financial burden of medical treatment, she noted that AB PM-JAY has completed eight years and has covered more than 62 crore beneficiaries, strengthening financial protection for people from poor and vulnerable backgrounds.

Smt. Patel further emphasized that AIIMS New Delhi must increasingly function as a national hub for capacity building and indigenous innovation. She emphasised that the impact of AIIMS should be measured not only by the number of patients treated on its campus but also by the national capacity it creates by training healthcare professionals and enabling AIIMS-level expertise to reach other parts of the country. She also stressed that research should bridge the gap between the laboratory and the patient and translate into clinical use and public benefit.

Smt. Patel also underlined the need for greater development, validation and implementation of indigenous medical technologies. She said that India cannot rely indefinitely on imported medical technologies and that academia, hospitals and Indian industry must work together to develop solutions suited to the country’s healthcare requirements. She called upon AIIMS “to contribute to an ecosystem in which India not only adopts advanced healthcare solutions but also develops them.”

Smt. Patel called for greater attention to the health and well-being of healthcare professionals themselves. She emphasised that along with treating patients, the health of doctors and other healthcare professionals is equally important for building a healthy nation. She stressed the importance of inculcating healthy habits among healthcare professionals from a young age and promoting a culture that supports their well-being.

Smt. Patel urged AIIMS New Delhi to continuously examine areas where improvements can be made. Looking ahead, Smt. Patel called upon AIIMS New Delhi “to play an even more commanding role in advanced clinical care, nurture the next generation of compassionate healthcare professionals, undertake research addressing India’s unique health challenges and guide the broader AIIMS network as a unified family of institutions.” She emphasised that the quality of care and expertise developed at AIIMS New Delhi should have a wider national impact.

Smt. Patel expressed appreciation for the entire AIIMS family, including doctors, nurses, researchers, students, technicians, pharmacists, administrators, sanitation workers and security personnel, and acknowledged their collective contribution to the institution’s achievements. She called for patient care to become more accessible, safer and increasingly patient-centred, while emphasising that technology should strengthen and not replace the human relationship at the core of healing.

In her concluding remarks, Smt. Patel stated that AIIMS New Delhi has a distinguished past and a strong present, but carries an even greater responsibility to shape the future of Indian healthcare. She called for the institution to continue serving as a beacon of excellence, trust, affordability, innovation and selfless service to the people of India.

Smt. Patel also distributed awards to outstanding performers in different fields during the event.

As part of the celebrations, Smt. Anupriya Patel also inaugurated the exhibition “AIIMS: Seven Decades of Healthcare Innovation”. The exhibition showcases the journey of AIIMS and its contributions to healthcare and medical innovation through 95 posters, highlighting important milestones, achievements, initiatives and developments across the institution.

The exhibition also focuses on health education and community outreach. More than 1,500 school students will visit the exhibition and engage with interactive displays and live demonstrations on BMI assessment, healthy lifestyle and nutrition, blood sugar testing, common eye problems, dental and oral hygiene, organ donation and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) to learn how to revive critically ill patients. The exhibition will remain open from 25th to 27th September 2026.

Addressing the gathering, Director, AIIMS New Delhi, Dr. (Prof.) Nikhil Tandon highlighted the institution’s extraordinary scale of patient care, noting that AIIMS New Delhi recorded more than 50 lakh outpatient visits, admitted over 3.5 lakh patients and conducted nearly 3 lakh surgeries during the past year. He emphasized that these figures reflected the immense trust placed by people across the country in the institution. He also highlighted major advances in clinical care, including the milestone of more than 1,000 robotic surgeries and the successful performance of India’s first reported robot-assisted kidney transplant in a public sector institution. AIIMS also doubled its dialysis capacity and undertook over 300 highly complex super-microsurgical procedures.

Dr. Tandon further highlighted AIIMS New Delhi’s growing national role in capacity building, digital health, research and indigenous innovation. He noted that the institution welcomed around 1,000 new students and recruited over 300 faculty members during the year. He emphasised that AIIMS must extend its expertise beyond its campus through digital health, telemedicine and capacity-building initiatives to strengthen healthcare delivery across the country.

Dr. Shyam Sunder Kothari, Former Professor and Head, Department of Cardiology, AIIMS, New Delhi, faculty members, students and staff of AIIMS New Delhi were present on the occasion.

headline: TDB-DST signs agreement with Agnikul Cosmos for ₹200 crore RDI support to develop fully reusable Agnibaan launch vehicle
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

TDB-DST signs agreement with Agnikul Cosmos for ₹200 crore RDI support to develop fully reusable Agnibaan launch vehicle

Project targets next-generation reusable launch capability, taking the technology from TRL-4 and above towards TRL-8

25 SEP 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi

India’s journey towards building a new generation of indigenous and reusable space transportation systems has received a significant boost with the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, signing an agreement with M/s Agnikul Cosmos Private Limited, Chennai, Tamil Nadu for ₹200 crore financial support under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

The project focuses on the development of a reusable launch vehicle – Agnibaan RLV, with the objective of taking the technology from TRL-4 and above to TRL-8. The financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCD). The project seeks to move beyond the conventional approach of recovering only the first stage of a launch vehicle and work towards full-system reusability. The proposed architecture is designed to enable high-frequency and repeatable launches while reducing launch and manufacturing costs and limiting the generation of space debris.

At the core of the programme is a reusable launch architecture combining a lightweight upper stage, precise orbital insertion capabilities and a semi-cryogenic liquid propulsion system designed for deep throttling and restart capability. The approach is intended to provide greater flexibility in mission operations while improving the potential for repeated use of the launch system.

Agnikul has already demonstrated several elements of the technology through its development and testing programmes. The company’s earlier work includes the development of Agnibaan, its indigenous orbital-class launch vehicle, and the Agnilet engine, a single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine developed and manufactured in-house. TDB had earlier supported Agnikul’s development and commercialisation of a modular configurable launch vehicle for small satellite missions.

The new RDI-supported programme takes this technology journey a step further — from developing a launch vehicle to developing a system designed around reusability, repeatability and operational efficiency. The proposed Agnibaan RLV incorporates a reusable upper-stage architecture and descent propulsion system, with the project envisaging technologies that can support controlled descent and recovery. The company’s development programme also includes propulsion systems capable of restart and deep throttling, critical capabilities for descent and landing operations.

The project is expected to support the development and validation of technologies required for a reusable launch architecture, including propulsion, ascent systems, orbital insertion, descent and recovery. The programme is aligned with the RDI Fund’s identified priority area of advanced and reusable launch vehicles and propulsion innovation within Space Technologies.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The next phase of India’s space journey will require technologies that not only reach orbit but can do so with greater frequency, flexibility and efficiency. Reusability is an important technology frontier in this regard. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting the development of ambitious indigenous technologies that require sustained investment to progress from advanced technology stages towards deployment. The Agnibaan RLV programme reflects this approach by focusing on the development of a reusable launch architecture and strengthening India’s capabilities in advanced space transportation systems.”

Promoters of Agnikul Cosmos Private Limited said, “Reusability requires the integration of propulsion, vehicle design, guidance, recovery and mission operations into a highly reliable system. TDB providing support for this is unique and special for us as it shows that the Government is willing to back original technology development in India. Such support will enable us to progress development of Agnibaan towards as a world class operational vehicle and build an indigenous platform for repeatable access to space.”

headline: A powerful punch by black hole jets shapes the fate of galaxies
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

A powerful punch by black hole jets shapes the fate of galaxies

25 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Astronomers have discovered a possible mechanism by which the black holes at the hearts of galaxies could be influencing the humongous, faint reservoir of gas surrounding their host galaxies, ultimately shaping the fates of galaxies.

When one thinks of a galaxy, one imagines dust and stars sparkling within beautiful spirals. But beyond the galactic disk’s edge lies a diffuse, ghostly envelope spreading out as far as 10–20 times the size of the galaxy. This gaseous reservoir is called the circumgalactic medium or CGM. This CGM provides the fuel for star formation.

But if all the gas existing within the boundary of the CGM did end up clumping together into stars, extremely luminous galaxies with a huge number of stars would form. But such galaxies don’t really exist. For more than a decade now, astronomers have proposed that energy from supermassive black holes (SMBHs) sitting at the hearts of galaxies could be preventing the gas from cooling and collapsing into stars. But there’s no consensus yet on how this may be happening. Before going into how, it helps to put into context the relative sizes of the SMBH and the galaxy to understand the scale of influence being talked about.

Though an average SMBH could be the size of the solar system, it is still tiny compared to the galaxy, which could host 100 billion such stellar systems.

A team of researchers from institutions like the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Arizona State University found one way in which the tiny black hole at the centre could energetically influence the ginormous CGM of its host galaxy.

While black holes conjure the image of monstrous voids gobbling up gas and dust from their surroundings, they also often burp out jets of seething hot plasma, which is a soup of charged particles. The team, composed of scientists from India and USA, explored if this jet modifies the gas all the way up to the CGM.

They found that when a jet from a black hole first encounters the CGM, it bumps on the gas in the CGM creating a jerk which kindles the gas. This bright, energised gas in the CGM can prevent star-formation in the galaxy.

Energised and ionized gas — gas that has atoms with electrons added or removed which imparts the atoms charge — emits a particular glow. The team looked for this glow in the CGM. They didn’t detect a signal when they averaged the measurements over all directions around the galaxies. “However, when we probed along the direction of the jet, we detected a strong signal.

This told us that the jet was illuminating only the gas in its path, rather than affecting the gas equally in all directions,” said Namrata Roy, assistant professor in the Astronomy and Astrophysics division at RRI and the lead author of the paper published today in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Further, they found that the signal is strongest in two places — at the edge of the stellar disk, where the jet first encounters the CGM, and next at the CGM’s outer boundary, where the already slowed down jet fist-bumps the gas in the CGM. This is akin to punching something hard and getting a jerk. There’s a deposition of energy, and this energy is what kindles the gas preventing star formation.

Fig. An artist’s impression of how relativistic jets launched by the central supermassive black holes (also known as an “active galactic nuclei”/AGN) impact the surrounding gaseous reservoir in a galaxy.

Image courtesy: Hailey Nelson, Arizona State University (ASU).

Cool gas clumps together to form stars. But the jet launched from the black hole fires up and disturbs the gas along its path, preventing it from clumping together and suppressing star formation. In this way, the black hole at the galaxy’s centre governs the galaxy’s fate, making it quiet and passive. “The wider implication is that black holes can shape the lives of galaxies far beyond the small central region where they sit,” says Sanchayeeta Borthakur, associate professor at Arizona State University and a co-author of this work. “[It’s like] the ant sitting in India is making a huge mark somewhere in the USA.”

For now, Roy, Borthakur and colleagues can take satisfaction in the fact that they did not miss the blazing trail this ant of a black hole left on the mammoth galaxy in which it resides.
